title: Hartmanis–Stearns conjecture
formal: For every integer \(b\ge 2\) and every real \(x\in\)[0,1), if a deterministic multitape Turing machine generates the base-b digits of x in order with a constant bound on the time between successive digits, must x be rational or transcendental?
why: A proof would impose a strong arithmetic restriction on numbers generated at the fastest possible asymptotic output rate. The checked 2024 source also records that the conjecture would rule out linear-time integer multiplication on multitape Turing machines.

progress.text: Linear-time and real-time sequence generation are shown to coincide for multitape machines.
The published revisiting paper proves transcendence restrictions for pushdown and exponential-growth morphic models.
ICALP work proves additional word-based transcendence results while explicitly retaining the full conjecture.
Automata compute digits from specially represented inputs; a June thesis abstract still describes the general conjecture as open.

references.title: On the computational complexity of algebraic numbers: the Hartmanis–Stearns problem revisited
references.authors: Boris Adamczewski; Julien Cassaigne; Marion Le Gonidec
references.locator: Bibliographic reference cited by the Wikipedia article; consult the original for definitions and assumptions.

references.title: Wikipedia: Hartmanis–Stearns conjecture
references.locator: Discovery source; retrieved 2026-09-11. Evidence locator: real-time

definitions: Write \(x=\sum _{n\ge 1}d_{n} b^{- n}\), where \(d_{n}\in \{0,\ldots ,b- 1\}\), using the unique expansion that is not eventually all \(b- 1; a\) terminating expansion continues with zeros. Rational means \(x=p/q\) for integers p,q with \(q\ne 0\). Algebraic means \(\mathrm{P}(x)=0\) for a nonzero polynomial P with integer coefficients; transcendental means not algebraic. A machine has a finite control, a fixed finite tape alphabet, and a fixed finite number of two-way infinite work tapes, each with one head and initially blank. Each transition reads the symbols under the heads, writes at those cells, changes state and moves each head at most one cell. It may also append one digit to a separate write-only output stream; written digits are irrevocable. It starts with no input and no advice or oracle and runs indefinitely. There must be a constant \(C\ge 1\) such that its first digit appears by step C and, writing \(t_{n}\) for the step at which \(d_{n}\) appears, \(1\le t_{n+1}- t_{n}\le C\) for every \(n\ge 1\). The finite machine and C may depend on the fixed x and b, but not on n. This is the constant-delay, or real-time, convention used by this card. Restricting to [0,1) only removes an integer part, which does not change rationality or transcendence.
answer_criterion: Prove the implication for all bases, numbers and machines just defined, or refute it by exhibiting an algebraic irrational x, a base b and a machine with proofs of correct infinite digit generation and a uniform constant delay. A computation of any finite prefix, a slower digit algorithm or a theorem restricted to finite automata does not settle the statement.

context_blocks.title: A steady stream of digits
context_blocks.text: For example, \(1/7=0.142857142857\ldots\) in base 10. A finite machine can cycle through the six-digit block forever with bounded delay. Every rational has an eventually periodic expansion, so rational numbers fit the model. In contrast, \(\sqrt{2}- 1\) is algebraic and irrational: it satisfies \(x^{2}+2x- 1=0\). The conjecture excludes such numbers from all constant-delay generators, even though their digits are computable.

context_blocks.title: The finite description is not the resource bound
context_blocks.text: The same program must produce the entire infinite expansion; it cannot receive a longer precomputed digit table for each requested precision. Work tapes may grow without bound. The restriction is how many elementary steps separate outputs, not a fixed bound on memory. No claim is made that every transcendental number has such a generator.

context_blocks.title: Why sources also say linear time
context_blocks.text: Fischer, Meyer and Rosenberg establish that linear-time and real-time sequence generation coincide for multitape Turing machines. This concerns the existence of a suitable generator; a particular implementation with linear total time need not itself have bounded gaps. The constant-delay wording therefore agrees with the linear-prefix formulation used in the cited Hartmanis–Stearns literature.

context_blocks.title: What the partial results establish
context_blocks.text: Adamczewski, Cassaigne and Le Gonidec exclude algebraic irrationals from several restricted generation models, including a deterministic pushdown transducer supplied with a digit index. Their one-stack theorem is not a theorem about arbitrary multitape generators. The 2024 ICALP paper likewise obtains transcendence for particular word classes and explicitly retains the full conjecture.

context_blocks.title: The input representation matters
context_blocks.text: The 2026 automata result obtains a digit of a quadratic irrational from \(b^{n}\) supplied in a special Ostrowski numeration system. This is additional structured input, whereas the machine in this card starts blank and produces digits indefinitely. The authors do not claim a fast general digit generator, so that result is not a counterexample.

sentences: The question concerns a fixed machine that prints all digits of a real number with bounded delay between outputs.
Every rational number permits this because its expansion is eventually periodic.
The conjecture says that any irrational number generated this quickly must be transcendental.
It quantifies over unrestricted deterministic multitape machines, beyond the restricted automata covered by known partial results.
A proof would connect the arithmetic nature of numbers to a stringent computation bound and rule out linear-time integer multiplication.
